physics_goals.value: Search for dark photons, light dark bosons (Z') and other dark-sector particles, and for invisible decays of neutral mesons, using the active beam-dump / missing-energy technique

summary.plain: NA64 is a CERN experiment that fires an electron beam into a block of material and watches for missing energy -- a sign that an invisible, unknown particle escaped. It searches for dark photons and other hidden particles.
summary.technical: Fixed-target active beam-dump experiment on the H4 beamline in EHN1 (CERN North Area SPS beam), using 100-150 GeV electrons (with planned muon/hadron beam extensions) and the missing-energy technique to search for dark photons, dark leptonic gauge bosons and invisible meson decays. Proposed January 2014, approved by the CERN Research Board 9 March 2016, operating since 2016.

unique_capabilities.value: Active beam-dump and missing-energy technique whose sensitivity to a hidden Z' coupling scales as ε² rather than ε⁴ as in classical beam-dump searches
